title: SEBI's Proposed PMS Changes: What They Mean for Your Portfolio

faq.q: What is a Portfolio Management Service (PMS)?
faq.a: A PMS is a professional service for managing an individual's investment portfolio, typically for high-net-worth individuals. Unlike mutual funds, it offers a more personalised and customised approach to investment management, tailored to specific client needs and risk profiles.

faq.q: What is the typical minimum investment for a PMS?
faq.a: Currently, the minimum investment for a PMS in India is ₹50 lakhs. However, SEBI's proposed changes might introduce specific product categories with potentially lower entry thresholds to attract a broader investor base.

faq.q: How do PMS fees generally work?
faq.a: PMS typically charges a combination of a fixed management fee (a percentage of the assets under management) and/or a performance-based fee (a percentage of returns above a certain hurdle rate). It's crucial to understand the fee structure before investing.

faq.q: How will SEBI's proposed changes benefit investors?
faq.a: The proposed changes are expected to introduce more diverse and specialised PMS products, such as thematic or asset allocation-focused strategies. This will provide investors with greater choice, more tailored solutions, and potentially better alignment with their specific financial goals.

faq.q: Will these changes make PMS riskier?
faq.a: While new products offer more choice, the underlying investment risks remain. Investors must carefully evaluate the risk profile of any new PMS product, understand its strategy, and ensure it aligns with their personal risk tolerance. Diversification and professional advice remain key.

faq.q: Where can I find official information on these proposed changes?
faq.a: Official information and final notifications regarding SEBI's regulatory changes are published on the official SEBI website. It is advisable to refer to these sources for accurate and up-to-date details.
